description: Water at the DALTON HF/aug-cc-pVQZ optimized geometry, HF, one rung (protocol 1e-4, k 6): alpha(0) xyz, the Raman component d alpha_zz/d z_O (raman.nuc_atom 0, axis 2) = 4.351172 au (row 8, A=z B=dipole_z C=nuc_0_z), two RPA excited states (omega 0.322390, 0.383291) and their 2PA D_linear (2.494093, 21.003235). The response block runs dconv 1e-4. It ran 1e-3 until the FD gate became relative (bsh <= 5 dconv (1 + ||x||), likewise for the density): under the old absolute bsh < 5*dconv the nuclear-displacement leg, ~1e3 larger than a dipole leg, plateaued near 4e-3 at 1e-4 and Raman was dropped. Now it converges in 22 iterations (the dipole legs 10-13), which sets the envelope's iteration count. Against the previous 1e-3 reference: alpha diag +1.6e-4 / -2.7e-3 / +4.7e-4, Raman -0.03 %, omega -3e-5 / -4e-5, D_linear +0.25 % / -0.11 %. Keeping the deck at 1e-3 under the relative gate would have moved Raman -0.9 %: rtol = 5 dconv = 5e-3 is too loose for a 1e3-norm leg. DALTON d-aug-cc-pVQZ at this geometry (refs h2o_hfopt): alpha diag 7.830/8.877/8.292, and the finite-difference d alpha_zz/d z_O is 4.28802 at protocol 1e-6/k8 -- both for reading, not asserted; nothing here is a converged number. Reference: RelWithDebInfo, Pthreads, ArmPL, 1 rank x 7 threads, dd (Neoverse-N1), 2026-09-27, on 0ecf076f3 plus the FD relative gate, wall 3480 s on a shared host (a 32-thread run reproduced it to 1e-10 in 2257 s). Nightly tier.
